questions.stem: A young sexually active female presented with a symptomatic UTI. Urinalysis and cultures showed novobiocin-resistant coagulase negative staphylococcus with a count of 10^4 cells/HPF. What is true about this condition?

options.label: B
options.text: Test must be repeated with a fresh specimen

options.label: C
options.text: Diagnose and treat as urinary tract infection

options.label: D
options.text: Normal skin commensal grown on culture that needed to proved

questions.answerText: Diagnose and treat as urinary tract infection
questions.solutionHtml:
Diagnose and treat as urinary tract infection
  • The given clinical scenario is suggestive of UTI caused by Staphylococcus saprophyticus, a common cause of UTI in sexually active young females.
  • Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a gram positive cocci which is non hemolytic, catalase positive and coagulase/DNase negative and Novobiocin resistant.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 563,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 752

questions.stem: A woman gave birth to a child 8 months after the death of her husband. The in-laws claim that the child is not their son, however, the DNA testing confirms the paternity. The child is known as ----------?
questions.solutionHtml:
Posthumous child
  • The child born after the death of the father is known as a posthumous child.


Reddy, KS Narayan; Murty, OP. The Essentials of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page No. 301, 309.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used for syndromic diagnosis of infected cases like meningitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiplex PCR
  • Advanced microbiology technologies such as multiplex molecular assays (i.e. syndromic diagnostic tests) are a novel approach to the rapid diagnosis of common infectious diseases including meningitis.
  • Multiplex PCR and multiplex real-time PCR can be used for simultaneous detection of common agents of
  • A meningitis/encephalitis (ME) panel is able to detect the most common bacterial, viral and fungal causes of community-acquired CNS infections concurrently with a single CSF sample.


Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 47-8, 695.

questions.stem: A patient receiving chemotherapy develops pneumonia with skin lesions. Microscopy of Specimen from skin lesions showed thick walled broad based budding yeast cells. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Blastomycosis

The given description classically describes Blastomyces dermatitidis, a dimorphic fungus and microscopy shows thick walled broad based budding yeast cells resembling a figure of 8 appearance.



Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 599-609., Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 574-583.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man came to the OPD with a febrile illness of 2 days, associated with abdominal tenderness, malaise and diarrhoea. He had a fever with bradycardia and BP was noted as 110/70 mmHg. He lives in a crowded neighbourhood with poor sanitation where many others have reported similar complaints recently. Which of the following investigations would be the most appropriate choice for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Blood culture
  • Blood and bone marrow culture are used for diagnosis of Typhoid or enteric fever in the first week of illness.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 298-302, Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 302-308.

questions.stemHtml: A child is brought with complaints of abdominal pain, diarrhoea and perianal itching for the last 3 days. The mother said she noticed a white thread- like structure in the child's night clothes. She collected the worm and brought it to the clinician. A perianal swab was collected. Microscopy of the swab and the worm are shown in the images. What is the likely causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Enterobius Vermicularis
  • The image shows an Enterobius adult worm and egg. Morphologic features of this nematode include the cervical alae in adult worms which is a wing-like expansion of cuticle near the anterior end.
  • vermicularis, the most common agent responsible for the helminthic infection in children, most common in the developed countries, usually produces pruritus ani as the outstanding and most disturbing symptom of Enterobiasis (pinworm infection).
  • In children with anal pruritus, the “Scotch tape” test can be used to help identify perianal eggs.


Essentials of Medical Parasitology, Apurba S Sastry, 2nd Edition, Page No. 137-151, 179-197.

questions.stem: A male patient comes to you with a history of UTI, the cause of which is suspected to be bacteria. Which of the following is used by the bacteria for adherence?UTI - Urinary Tract Infection
questions.solutionHtml:
Fimbriae
  • Fimbriae or pili are short, fine, hair-like appendages which are organs of adhesion that help in bacterial adhesion.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, Lange McGraw Hill Publications, 28th Edition, Page No. 238., Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 21-22., Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 17-20.

questions.stem: A Thalassemia patient has received multiple blood transfusions. Aplastic crisis can occur in this patient due to infection from?
questions.solutionHtml:
Parvovirus
  • Aplastic crisis can occur in the patient in the scenario mentioned above, which is usually due to parvovirus B19 infection of erythroid precursor cells in the bone marrow.
  • Parvovirus is a nonenveloped single-stranded DNA virus. Destruction of the erythroid precursor cells by this virus diminishes the number of reticulocytes available to replace the deformed and/or removed erythrocytes.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th Edition, Lange McGraw Hill Publications, Page No. 780, Ananthanarayan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 589, Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition. Page No. 556-7.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old farmer comes with complaints of high-grade fever with chills, retro- orbital pain and conjunctival suffusion. On examination, he has severe calf tenderness. Lab examination shows hypokalemia and neutropenia. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leptospirosis
  • The symptoms of leptospirosis, a zoonotic infection, can vary widely, ranging from mild to severe. Fever, myalgia, headache/retro orbital pain, conjunctival suffusion etc are seen in initial states of Leptospira infection. The occupational history provides a clue of acquiring infection through water contaminated with rodents urine.
  • High grade fever, jaundice (5–10%) and raised liver enzymes, hemorrhagic manifestations and renal involvement seen as raised serum urea and creatinine and renal failure are clinical features seen in Weil’s disease.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 306-8.,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 317-24.

questions.stem: A patient with a history of consumption of oysters comes with complaints of nausea, vomiting and crampy abdominal pain. The culture of the organism showed the Kanagawa phenomenon. What is the causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vibrio parahaemolyticus
  • Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a halophilic bacterium that causes acute gastroenteritis following ingestion of contaminated seafood such as raw fish or shellfish.
  • After 12-24 hours, the patient develops nausea and vomiting, abdominal cramps, fever, and watery to bloody diarrhea. It is usually self-limited in 1-4 days, requiring only restoration of water and electrolytes.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 477.,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 410-17.

questions.stem: A man is having petechial rashes with a previous history of meningitis. He was vaccinated at the age of 5 years. Now, Brudzinski and Kernig's signs were positive. Microscopy showed gram negative diplococci. What is the likely causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Neisseria Meningitidis
  • It’s a case of N meningitidis infection resulting in meningitis, with prominent hemorrhagic skin lesions as per given clinical presentation. Meningitis with hemorrhagic rash is seen in N. Meningitidis


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 434-7.,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 695-7.

questions.stem: A patient who has a central line on long-term IV antibiotics develops a fever. Blood cultures show Staphylococcus epidermidis along with biofilm formation. Which of the following describes its features of antibiotic resistance?

options.label: B
options.text: Biofilm offers resistance so catheter is to be removed

options.label: C
options.text: Biofilm does not affect susceptibility to antibiotics

options.label: D
options.text: Biofilm can be washed off from the catheter, hence catheter need not to be removed

questions.answerText: Biofilm offers resistance so catheter is to be removed
questions.solutionHtml:
Biofilm offers resistance so catheter is to be removed
  • Most bacteria live in complex communities called biofilms.
  • A biofilm is a well-organized community of bacteria that adheres to surfaces and is embedded in an extracellular slime layer.
  • Once a bacterium attaches to a surface, it activates a whole different set of genes that gives the bacterium different characteristics from those that it had as a free-floating organism.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 120,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 69, 243, 518, 643

questions.stem: Laboratory investigations in a patient with desert rheumatism showed dimorphic and thermal fungi with arthrospores. What is the causative organism of desert rheumatism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Coccidioides immitis
  • Desert rheumatism is caused by Coccidioides immitis.
  • This organism is an endemic dimorphic fungus found in the desert southwest.
  • Its arthroconidia are spread in blowing dust and transmission occurs by inhalation.
  • Those at risk of serious infection include the elderly and immunocompromised individuals. In these persons, a progressive pulmonary infection with cavitary lesions can result.
  • Diagnosis can be accomplished by the finding of characteristic spherules containing endospores in the sputum.
  • None of the other fungi listed form these characteristic spherules, although all of them can cause pulmonary infections.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th Edition, Lange McGraw Hill Publications, Page No. 690-700,Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 413-14,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 379-83

questions.stemHtml: A farmer from South East India presents with fever, respiratory distress and neurological deficits. The vector of the causative organism is shown below. What is the associated organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nipah virus
  • Transmission of Nipah virus to humans may occur after direct contact with infected fruit bats, pigs, or persons. Nipah virus was first discovered in 1999 in Malaysia.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 378.,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition. Page No. 718.

questions.stemHtml: A middle-aged man presented to the OPD with dysuria and purulent urethral discharge for the last 3 days. Gram stain of the discharge is shown below. He admits to having unprotected sexual intercourse one week ago. What is the most appropriate treatment?

options.label: A
options.text: Tab. Acyclovir 500 mg TDS for 1 week

options.label: B
options.text: Tab. Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days

options.label: D
options.text: Inj. Benzathaine Penicillin 2.4 MU IM Stat

questions.solutionHtml:
Tab. Cefixime 400 mg Stat
  • The given clinical vignette is suggestive of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection which is a non-capsulated, gram-negative kidney-shaped diplococcus.
  • Causes ‘gonorrhea’, a sexually transmitted infection (STI) - commonly manifests as cervicitis, urethritis and conjunctivitis.
  • Third generation cephalosporins – DOC for uncomplicated gonococcal infection -
    • Ceftriaxone (250 mg given IM, single dose)
    • Cefixime (400 mg given orally, single dose)


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 541-43.,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 764-766.

questions.stem: A group of hostel boys consumed hamburgers from a local street food shop following which they developed abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, and fever. They were diagnosed with hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS). Escherichia coli O157:H7 was detected in the stool samples and the ham. What does H represent in H7?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flagella
  • Enterohemorrhagic E.coli dysentery can lead to complications like hemorrhagic uremic syndrome and hemorrhagic colitis.
  • Serotypes’ associated with EHEC are O157: H7 and O26:H1
  • Similar illness also produced by Shigella dysenteriae type1.
  • H refers to flagellar antigen


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 32-35.Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 20-21.

questions.stem: A young man presents with burning and painful micturition. Microscopy showed gram-negative intracellular kidney bean-shaped organisms. Which of the following culture media is used to isolate the organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thayer-Martin media
  • The given clinical vignette is suggestive of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection which is a non capsulated, gram-negative kidney-shaped diplococcus.
  • Causes ‘gonorrhea’, a sexually transmitted infection (STI) - commonly manifests as cervicitis, urethritis and conjunctivitis.
  • As cervical swabs contain normal flora - selective media is used for culture to inhibit commensal Neisseria, Thayer Martin medium - A chocolate agar with antibiotics.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presented with high fever, bleeding gums, myalgia, and hepatosplenomegaly. His TLC is 3100, Hb- 11 g/dl, hematocrit- 55%, and platelets - 25,000 cells. What is the most important prognostic factor in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hematocrit
  • A hematocrit level increase of 20% or more is a sign of hemoconcentration and can precede shock. In severe cases of dengue, hematocrit levels should be monitored every 3-4 hours,

questions.stem: A 22-year-old farmer develops an ulcer on his foot with a white powdery substance and multiple discharging sinuses. Microscopy reveals a gram- positive organism with radiating filaments. What is the most likely organism isolated from the discharging sinus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nocardia
  • The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Mycetoma. Gram positive organisms with radiating filaments are suggestive of Nocardia spp. and mycetoma being Actinomycetoma.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 581-2,Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 542-5

questions.stem: An elderly female with a central line undergoes surgery. On postoperative day 3, she develops fever and tachycardia. A culture from the tip of the central line revealed brown buff colonies. Microscopy showed gram-positive organisms that reproduce by budding. What is the likely causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Candida
  • The given clinical vignette is suggestive of central line associated bloodstream infection by Candida sp. which is seen as gram positive budding yeast cells in microscopy.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 320.Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 378.

questions.stem: A middle-aged man presents with complaints of itching around the perianal region and unilateral lower limb lymphadenopathy. Larvae of approximately 200 microns in size were identified, and these larvae lacked nuclei at their tail tips. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Wuchereria Bancrofti
  • Microfilaria are differentiated on the basis of presence of sheath and tail tip characteristics.
  • Sheathed microfilaria: W. bancrofti, Brugia malayi and Loa loa.
    • Nuclei extending upto tail tip: Loa loa
    • Nuclei, two widely spaced in tail tip: Brugia
    • No nuclei in tail region: Wuchereria


Essentials of Medical Parasitology, Apurba S Sastry, 2nd Edition, Page No. 210-223.Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 370-76.

questions.stemHtml: A young man who has just returned from the USA develops fever, cough, and breathlessness. A chest radiograph shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Culture on Sabouraud Dextrose Agar (SDA) reveals white to light brown puffy colonies. Lactophenol blue staining shows the findings as depicted in the image. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Histoplasmosis
  • The tuberculate macroconidia are seen in the above given microscopic culture picture  which is characteristic of Histoplasma.

Histoplasma:

  • Histoplasma capsulatum is a dimorphic fungus.
  • It is non-capsulated (Only medically important capsulated fungus is Cryptococcus).
  • Infectious form is microconidia (small spores) and mode of transmission is inhalation of dust contaminated with bird or bat dropping.
  • It causes intracellular infection of reticuloendothelial system.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 599-609.Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 574-583.

questions.stemHtml: A child presented with diarrhea and dehydration. There was no blood in the stools. A stool examination revealed a spoke wheel pattern. Identify the causative organism.
questions.solutionHtml:
Rota Virus
  • The image given shows the characteristic picture of Rotaviruses with typical spoke wheel pattern. Rotavirus are the most common cause of diarrheal illness in infants and children all over the world.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 498.Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 424-25.

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with HIV presents with complaints of recurrent diarrhoea. The stool sample reveals only larvae and no ova. Which of the following is the most probable causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Strongyloides
  • Strongyloides stercoralis is an ovoviviparous organism, larvae immediately hatches out from eggs, therefore stool examination reveals larvae (rhabditiform). Presentation of Strongyloides in patients with AIDS must be distinguished from Ancylostoma spp./Necator spp.
  • By microscopy, later showing presence of non-bile stained eggs with segmented ovum. Gross appearances can be similar.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Lange McGraw Hill Publications, Page No. 747, Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 594, Essentials of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 457-68
